If we plug in $x=1$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)}{{x}^{2}-2x+1} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{[2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)]^{′}}{[{x}^{2}-2x+1]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{-2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)}{2x-2} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)}{x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)}{{x}^{2}-2x+1} & =-{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)}{x-1} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{[\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)]^{′}}{[x-1]^{′}} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{\pi }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)}{1} \\  & =-{\pi }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi  \\  & ={\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
